items.title: Vercel for Enterprise
items.summary: AI adoption in the enterprise is growing rapidly, and expanding beyond engineering users. In the last three months, token usage by enterprise companies on AI Gateway has quadrupled, and  that from August 2025 to June 2026, non-developer Codex users grew 189x. OpenAI recently reportedOur customers call these builders citizen developers. They know their part of the business better than anyone else, and with AI they can create the software they need to ship work faster and deliver better customer experiences.Building has never been easier, but that also means that control and governance have never been harder. Employees are using AI tools , and if a citizen developer vibe codes a login page incorrectly, private data can reach the public internet.whether they are approved or notEnterprise leaders have to figure out how to let everyone build, without giving up security or control.We built Enterprise Apps and Agents to solve these challenges at Vercel, and in June, we  to our customers. Enterprise Apps and Agents is a central control plane for governing every builder, app, agent, token, and dollar.made it availableToday, we are expanding the platform:Enterprise Apps and Agents gives you a single deployment destination for both engineers and citizen developers, with central governance over access, providers, models, data retention, token budgets, integrations, and policies, managed through your existing IdP.Vercel centralizes AI governance so that company policies can be applied consistently across control domains. Apps and agents run on the same infrastructure that powers billions of production deployments, and Vercel gives you a single place for  and security monitoring across every project, through , , and the .observabilityanalyticsaudit logsSecurity Dashboard provides private connectivity to enterprise systems, while BYOC on AWS lets your application functions run in your own AWS account under your permissions and network controls.Secure ComputeCitizen developers and engineers use different tools. A marketer might use ChatGPT to build a landing page, an analyst might use Claude Code to run queries and build a report, and an engineer might use Codex, OpenCode, or fx.No matter the harness, Vercel gives you a single deployment target, and connects to your existing IdP, so you can control who creates deployments. Before Vercel, shipping a simple internal app at Klaviyo took two weeks of chasing IT, opening tickets for engineering, and following up with the platform team. They built an internal app-building platform on top of Enterprise Apps and Agents, and now anyone in the company can deploy an idea in three minutes. In their first two weeks on Vercel, 512 employees deployed 356 apps.Controlling who can deploy doesn't protect the apps, agents, and data that make it into production.On Vercel, you can configure every deployment to be private by default, and with Vercel Passport, you can require employees to authenticate through your IdP before they can access internal apps.Agents are only useful when they can access your systems and data, but that often means using long-standing environment varibles with wide-ranging permissions to your CRM, databases, Slack, and other systems.Vercel Connect implements connectors with scoped access, and mints tokens for each agent task, meaning agents only access the specific context they need for the job. And now, with Enterprise-Managed Authorization, when employees sign into Vercel through your IdP, agents can use connected services automatically, without a separate authorization prompt.Connect also integrates with Passport, so individual employee permissions also apply at the integration and data layer. If someone can't see data in a source system, they can't access it through an app or agent either. The average enterprise company using Vercel AI Gateway routes across 17 different models. Without a model router, that would require integrating with multiple separate providers, spreading API keys and budget management across platforms.AI Gateway gives you access to hundreds of models through a single API, with no markup on cost, and Zero Data Retention keeps your data from being stored or trained on. You can also elect to route through US-only providers to maintain compliance.Mercor connects AI labs with subject-matter experts who help train and evaluate models. Their engineers need access to hundreds of models to enable that work, but before migrating to Vercel, access was spread across direct integrations and third-party routers, making stolen credentials a huge risk, and token spend impossible to manage.They moved their model routing to AI Gateway, and now engineers can access hundreds of models with a single, expiring secret, and they can set budgets per person or project.In their first 10 days on AI Gateway, they processed 63 billion tokens without hitting any rate limits. gives you a single view for app and agent telemetry across every project, so you can easily manage per

items.title: Introducing Vercel Drives: persistent storage for agents
items.summary: Agents often handle complex work that continues across runs. As that work evolves, they may need a new environment with different tools, runtimes, or compute. They should be able to continue working with the same files when they change environments.We built  to keep an agent’s files independent of its execution environment. It is now generally available for . Agents can mount the same drive in a new environment configured for the next task and continue where they left off.Vercel DrivesVercel SandboxCreate a drive once, then mount it when you create a sandbox. From the CLI:Or from the Sandbox SDK:In this example, everything under  persists on the drive. Everything else belongs to the sandbox. The next sandbox that mounts the drive finds the repository, and anything else the agent wrote there, where the previous run left it./workspaceThe drive keeps the agent’s files independent of the sandbox running it. An agent can resume work in a new sandbox or switch runtimes without transferring its workspace. Other sandboxes can mount the same drive.Agents can prepare files on a drive once and reuse them across sandboxes. If one agent builds a dataset on a drive, other agents can mount read-only copies to analyze the data or generate reports without rebuilding the dataset. They use the shared files as input and save their results separately.Agents can also fork a drive to explore different approaches independently. Each fork starts with the drive’s contents and provides its own writable workspace. Agents can try different transformations of the dataset in parallel without changing the original or affecting one another. Forks don’t merge back into the original drive.Forking is .generally availableVercel Drives is now generally available for Vercel Sandbox on all plans. Drives default to 1 TiB, or 1 GiB on Hobby, with up to 16 TiB available. Since container support entered Public Beta, 5,000 teams have shipped 150,000 container deployments on Vercel.Vercel container runtimeContainers deploy as Vercel Functions on Fluid compute, scaling with traffic and using , which doesn’t charge for idle time spent waiting for API responses, database queries, or LLM inferencing. items.title: Python on Vercel is now generally available
items.summary: Python on Vercel is now generally available. Build and run Python applications with the frameworks, libraries, and tools you already use.Vercel automatically detects supported frameworks and configures the build and deployment. Your applications run on Fluid compute, which manages concurrent requests and scales with traffic. Idiomatic Python SDKs let you work with storage, queues, durable workflows, and AI models directly from Python. For full-stack projects, the Python backend and frontend share a workflow for local development, preview deployments, and production releases.Ten months ago, we . We wanted the experience to fit how Python developers already work, with three goals guiding our decisions:set out to make Vercel the best place to build and run Python applicationsThe first test of those goals is what happens when you deploy a Python application on Vercel: its framework, dependencies, and project structure should guide how it’s built and run.We’ve worked to make Python feel native on Vercel. Vercel reads your project’s dependency files, including those managed by , and automatically detects frameworks such as FastAPI, Flask, Django, and FastHTML.  configures builds and request routing, with framework-specific support for serving static assets through the CDN.uvFramework defined infrastructureFor applications with a frontend,  brings both parts into one project. Running  starts them together, and shared previews let you test backend changes with the frontend that uses them.Vercel Servicesvercel devFor long-running workers that pull jobs from queues or databases,  keeps your containers running with your Python code along with any of its packages, and system dependencies.Vercel DaemonsA Python backend might need to store files, send messages, run durable workflows, or call AI models. We’ve built Python SDKs for these tasks, with APIs that follow the conventions of the language:These SDKs work alongside your framework and libraries, and the example below shows how they connect within a full-stack application.Whether you’re starting a new project or deploying existing code, the  cover setup and deployment on Vercel. For a guided full-stack project, the  walks through building a FastAPI backend and Next.js frontend, then deploying them together with Services.framework guidesPython on Vercel courseTo show how these pieces work together, I built a collaborative web application to create and browse Python notebooks. It lets people create their own notebooks, publish them for others to browse or fork, and work with an AI assistant to write and run Python code.The application pairs a Vite frontend with a FastAPI backend and uses PostgreSQL for notebook source and chat history. Services keeps the frontend and backend in one deployment, with the frontend served through the CDN.Here’s how the main parts connect:The  includes the complete application and its deployment configuration. You can use it to explore these integrations or as a starting point for your own Python application.source code on GitHubLast December, the Gel Data team, led by me and Elvis Pranskevichus,  to build Python support and continue our open-source work.joined VercelAt the same time, we announced our sponsorship of the Python Software Foundation and committed to funding one year of Serhiy Storchaka’s CPython maintenance through the foundation. Serhiy has authored over 600 commits to CPython’s main branch so far in 2026.We also sponsored PyCon US and EuroPython this year, where the team and I met Python developers and heard where they were getting stuck. Those conversations help us figure out what to fix next.We also published , which, if accepted, would add type manipulation features that could help frameworks such as FastAPI offer simpler APIs with less boilerplate and more precise type checking.PEP 827We’re continuing to improve Python SDKs, runtime performance, and development workflows for both people and coding agents. If you run into a deployment issue or find something missing in the Python SDKs,  so the team can use it to guide that work.share your feedback in Vercel CommunityRead moreOur goals for Python on VercelDeploying Python applications on VercelPython SDKs for Vercel infrastructureStart building with Python on VercelInvesting in the Python communityWhat’s next for Python on Vercel Working with Vercel infrastructure should feel familiar to Python developers, with APIs that use type annotations, /, and context managers.Idiomatic Python SDKs.asyncawait Python applications often include a JavaScript frontend, so developers should be able to run both locally, review them in the same preview deployment, and release or roll them back together.A shared workflow for both the frontend and backend. The runtime should use CPython, the standard Python interpreter, on Linux to preserve compatibility with the packages and tools Python developers already rely on.Compatibility with the Python ecosystem.
